reasons: The cited clause (§14) carries workers' compensation, CGL USD 1M, E&O USD 1M and certificates on request, but contains no cyber/privacy coverage at all; the fallback requires E&O USD 1M *and* cyber USD 2M, so the clause fails the fallback on a material term and 'deviation' is the correct classification rather than compliant.

Materiality is adequately grounded: Contractor obtains Company data and records (Confidential Information definition) and may access Company facilities/systems, which is precisely the fact pattern the rule's cyber requirement and walk-away language address.

The redline is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position — a single scoped insertion of cyber/privacy liability at USD 5,000,000 into the existing sentence, leaving the negotiated WC, CGL, E&O and certificate mechanics untouched; the high changed-character ratio is an artifact of inserting into one long sentence and not evidence of an over-broad rewrite.

Directionally correct for the customer (adds vendor-side coverage), and the comment accurately states what changed, cites the USD 5M preferred position and offers the USD 2M fallback in the required concise, first-person-plural tone with the [Playbook] prefix.
Correctly treats the absent CGL aggregate, E&O at fallback USD 1M and the lack of a one-year tail as noted-not-flagged sub-elements rather than separate deviations, avoiding over-flagging.
